persona_summary: CS Senior, dual minors BA + History, 60 courses, Good standing
question: I've completed 60 courses — I'm pretty sure I've covered everything for my CS degree and both minors. Can you confirm I'm good to graduate?
false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: With 60 courses, it seems like everything should be covered. But with dual minors, there's a risk that some courses are being double-counted (e.g., a course counting for both BA minor and CS gen-ed, or for both minors). A careful audit might reveal that after properly assigning courses to slots without double-counting violations, one requirement is still unmet.
naive_system_response: A naive system does a surface check, sees 60 courses with relevant course codes, and confirms 'You're all set to graduate!' — not doing a proper slot-by-slot audit.
correct_response: Let me do a careful audit of your 60 courses against all requirements: CS major [X/Y satisfied], BA minor [X/Y satisfied], History minor [X/Y satisfied], gen-ed [X/Y satisfied]. After assigning courses to their proper slots — ensuring no double-counting violations — I find: [result]. [If gap found]: You're missing [specific requirement] because [course X] was counted toward [program A] and cannot also count toward [program B].
why_multi_agent_helps: The Programs Agent audits each program independently. The Policy Agent enforces double-counting rules. The coordinator synthesizes the audits to find conflicts. A single agent might do a quick scan and confirm without the careful slot assignment.
key_facts: 60 courses seems like more than enough, creating overconfidence
Dual minors + major creates many overlapping requirement lists
Double-counting rules may mean some courses can't serve dual purposes
One hidden gap can block graduation
known_traps: Confirming graduation readiness based on course count rather than slot-by-slot audit
Not checking double-counting across three program requirement sets
advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) complete slot-by-slot audit of P-044's courses against CS + BA minor + History minor + gen-ed, (2) double-counting policy, (3) whether any gap exists after proper assignment
